Lazy random vectors

Source: R/lazy.R
rng_lazy_normal.Rd

rng_lazy_uniform() and rng_lazy_normal() return a numeric vector of length n whose elements are computed only when read. Every value is a pure function of the key and its position, so element i is exactly element i of rng_uniform(key, n, ...) or rng_normal(key, n, ...), and identical(x[], rng_normal(key, n)) holds. Creating one is instant and takes no memory for the values, whatever n is: each lazy vector holds its key, its arguments and a cache of one engine chunk, which is min(n, 5120) doubles, so at most about 40 KB.

Usage

rng_lazy_normal(key, n, mean = 0, sd = 1, method = c("ziggurat", "mcfarland"))

rng_lazy_uniform(key, n, min = 0, max = 1)

Arguments

key

A single rng_key.

n

A single non-negative whole number. Defaults to one draw per key.

mean

A single finite numeric mean.

sd

A single non-negative finite numeric standard deviation.

method

The sampling algorithm:

  • "ziggurat" (the default): Marsaglia and Tsang's ziggurat on NumPy's 256-layer tables.

  • "mcfarland": McFarland's modified ziggurat (2016). Its common case needs no table comparison, so it is faster than the default on every CPU measured, by more on x86_64 than on arm64 (vignette("performance", package = "zurand")).

Both are exact samplers of the standard normal (to double precision) and both are bit-reproducible across platforms. They are different streams: the same key gives unrelated values under the two methods, and changing the method changes every value. The default never changes.

min, max

Single finite numeric bounds.

Value

A double vector of length n (an ALTREP object).

Reading

x[i], x[idx], x[a:b], sum(x), mean(x) and loops over x compute only the values they touch; nothing is kept but the last engine chunk read (at most 5120 values), so sum() over 1e9 lazy values runs in the memory R itself uses. Full scans cost more than rng_normal() followed by sum() would, because R reads lazy vectors 512 values at a time on one thread. The gain is memory, and not paying for values that are never read.

Interrupts

Scans that read a lazy vector in blocks – sum(), mean(), max(), x[idx] – check for a user interrupt every \(2^{22}\) values, so Ctrl-C stops sum() over 1e12 values. Reading single elements and materialising do not check. For C and C++ code this means that REAL_ELT() and REAL()/REAL_RO() on a lazy vector never signal an interrupt, but REAL_GET_REGION() – which cpp11's doubles iterator uses – can, by a longjmp that skips C++ destructors. Code that cannot be unwound should take the data pointer first (which materialises the vector) or read under R_UnwindProtect() (cpp11::unwind_protect()).

Materialisation

Anything that needs the whole vector as ordinary memory – most arithmetic such as x * 2, modifying x, or C code asking for its data pointer – fills it once, with the usual parallel fill, and from then on x holds all n values like any vector.

Saving

saveRDS() and serialize() store only the key and the arguments, so a lazy vector of 1e9 values saves as a few hundred bytes and comes back lazy. A lazy vector that has been modified saves its values. Reading is not modifying: after C code has had the data pointer (sd(), sort() and cumsum() all take it), saving regenerates the values and compares them with what the vector holds, which costs about one more fill, and stores only the key when nothing changed. Restoring checks the saved arguments and refuses ones it cannot have written.

Engines

The vector uses its key's engine, so its values are that engine's. For scattered reads, x[sample(n, k)] or random indices in a loop, key it with rng_key(seed, engine = "philox4x64"): Philox computes any single value directly, several times faster per read than "xoshiro256pp", which reaches it through its 512-value block. For scans and sequential loops the default is faster.

Examples

key <- rng_key(42L)
x <- rng_lazy_normal(key, 1e9)      # instant; no values yet
x[c(1, 5e8, 1e9)]
#> [1]  1.6306140 -0.1649847  1.0731953
identical(rng_lazy_normal(key, 10)[], rng_normal(key, 10))
#> [1] TRUE
